en.title: Count Syllables and Mark Stress
en.summary: Learn to clap each Romanian syllable and emphasize the stressed beat for natural rhythm and clear pronunciation.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: Words have rhythm. Each syllable is a beat. Listen to (dimineață) /di.mi.ˈɲa.tsə/, which means morning. It has four beats. One beat is louder and stronger than the others. We call this strong beat the stress.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Clap your hands for every beat in a word. Say (dimineață) /di.mi.ˈɲa.tsə/ slowly. Clap four times. Make the third beat louder and longer. Open your mouth wider on that beat. Let your voice jump higher there. The other beats stay soft and short.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Look at (copil) /ko.ˈpil/, which means child. It has two beats. The stress lands on the second beat. Now look at (apă) /ˈa.pə/, which means water. The stress lands on the first beat. Romanian does not write stress marks on words. You must learn the rhythm of each word.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make every beat equal. A flat rhythm sounds strange and robotic. Do not swallow the weak syllables. Say every beat clearly, even the soft ones. Always hit the stressed beat firmly. If you stress the wrong syllable, people might not understand you.
